question: On a file inside the effective READ lane but outside the effective WRITE lane, does an UNDECLARED `chmod 600` still change the mode (Landlock has no chmod right, so the declaration is the only layer that could refuse it)?

observed.note: The fixture file was created and stat-ed by the driver before boot, but the home was deleted by teardown and no chmod call was ever made.

priorRecordOnThisQuestion.recorded: Undeclared `chmod` is not mediated by Landlock: Landlock has no 'change mode' right at all, so a same-uid inode the shell can reach can be chmod-ed even if the composition did not declare it. This is why chmod targets are a DECLARATION (consulted on the write lane).
priorRecordOnThisQuestion.status: host-free disclosure, not a live measurement

plannedObservable: stat mode before the call and after the call
the mode changes to 0600 although the composition declared no chmod target
the call itself is admitted (it declares a read inside the read lane), so the refusal cannot come from admission
whatWouldProveIt: modeBefore != modeAfter and modeAfter == 0o600, with the call's own exit code and stdout recorded

a declared-chmod negative control on a second file (`chmod` target outside the write lane) showing `IO_WRITE_DENIED`, 0 spawns, mode AND bytes unchanged — so the gap is shown to be the absence of a chmod right, not a broken declaration path
the result recorded whether or not it matches the a5sf-bash §6.2 prediction; a NOT-REPRODUCED would be as reportable as a GAP-REPRODUCED
honestLimits: No measurement was taken on this tree. The §6.2 record above remains the only statement, and it is host-free.

A future reproduction would prove a same-UID mode change outside the declared write lane; it would NOT prove that a confined face can read the file, and it would not change any matrix grade by itself.
